relationships.description: Connects Hybrid Vector & Keyword Search to llm prompt engineering in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: Combining sparse lexical scoring (BM25) with dense semantic embeddings (HNSW) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and cross-encoder reranking.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of hybrid search—from why dense vectors miss exact SKUs and error codes to RRF (k=60), single-stage filtered HNSW, and int8 scalar quantization.

spark.summary: Hybrid vector search combines sparse lexical scoring (BM25) with dense semantic embeddings (HNSW/IVF) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and optional cross-encoder reranking to achieve high recall on both exact identifiers and conceptual queries.
spark.keyTakeaway: Dense vectors alone miss exact SKUs, error codes, and proper nouns, while BM25 misses synonyms; run both in parallel, fuse with RRF (k=60), and cross-encoder rerank only the top 20–50 candidates.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Pure dense vector search embeds queries into 768–1536D vectors (indexed in **HNSW** graphs for `~10 ms` ANN lookup) and excels at paraphrases—but routinely misses exact tokens like `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` or `SKU-4920B`.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Parallel BM25 + HNSW -> RRF Fusion (k=60) -> Cross-Encoder Top-50 (User Query -> BM25 + HNSW Parallel -> RRF Fusion (k=60) -> Cross-Encoder Rerank); Hybrid Search Execution with Oversampling & Reranking (Search API -> BM25 + int8 HNSW -> RRF + Rescore -> GPU Cross-Encoder).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Compare fusion strategies and sparse-dense architectures. To keep 1536-dim HNSW indexes affordable in RAM, production clusters (Qdrant, OpenSearch, pgvector) apply **int8 scalar quantization** (4x RAM reduction) and oversample top-100.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore the inverted-index foundations behind BM25 and production search pagination.

learningJourney.title: What is Hybrid Vector Search
learningJourney.explanation:
Pure dense vector search embeds queries into 768–1536D vectors (indexed in **HNSW** graphs for `~10 ms` ANN lookup) and excels at paraphrases—but routinely misses exact tokens like `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` or `SKU-4920B`. Conversely, **BM25** nails exact rare tokens via inverted indexes but misses synonyms.

**Hybrid search** runs both retrievers in parallel and merges their ranked lists using **Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)**: `RRF(d) = sum(1 / (k + rank_i(d)))` (typically `k = 60`), requiring zero brittle score normalization between unbounded BM25 scores and `[0, 1]` cosine similarities.

cards.detail: Evaluates tenant/stock bitsets *inside* HNSW traversal so selective filters never return 0 results.

learningJourney.title: Why Post-Filtering & Naive Score Addition Fail
learningJourney.explanation: Two classic traps ruin hybrid search: (1) **Post-filtering** runs HNSW top-20 first and then applies `WHERE in_stock = true`—returning 0 results if the top-20 were out of stock; and (2) **Naive score addition** (`bm25 + cosine`) lets unbounded BM25 scores (`0..40+`) drown out cosine (`0..1`).

ideas.title: Structure-Aware Chunking
ideas.description: Split docs on Markdown/HTML headings with 10–15% overlap and prepend the document title/breadcrumb to each chunk so embeddings never lose context.

ideas.title: Cross-Encoder Precision
ideas.description: Bi-encoders encode query and doc separately; a cross-encoder runs full attention over `(query, doc)` pairs on just the top 20–50 RRF candidates to resolve negation and subtle nuance.

learningJourney.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) & Single-Stage Filtered Retrieval
learningJourney.explanation: Implement RRF with `k = 60` so documents appearing near the top of *both* BM25 and HNSW lists receive a strong boost without tuning per-corpus alpha weights.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```python
from collections import defaultdict

def reciprocal_rank_fusion(
    bm25_ids: list[str],
    vector_ids: list[str],
    k: int = 60,
    top_n: int = 20,
) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
    scores: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    for rank, doc_id in enumerate(bm25_ids, start=1):
        scores[doc_id] += 1.0 / (k + rank)
    for rank, doc_id in enumerate(vector_ids, start=1):
        scores[doc_id] += 1.0 / (k + rank)
    return sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:top_n]
```

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: RRF vs. Linear Alpha Fusion vs. Learned Sparse (SPLADE)
learningJourney.explanation: Compare fusion strategies and sparse-dense architectures.

benefits: Zero score calibration needed; resilient to BM25's unbounded `[0, inf)` range.
costs: Discards score magnitude gaps (a `0.99` exact hit vs. a `0.51` weak hit look identical at rank 1).

benefits: Preserves score confidence gaps when scores are min-max or z-score normalized per query.
costs: Requires domain-specific tuning of `alpha` and breaks if score distributions shift.

benefits: Highest precision on top-50 candidates via full query-document token attention.
costs: Adds 40–150 ms GPU latency (200+ ms CPU); unsuitable for sub-20 ms autocomplete.

learningJourney.title: Production Search: Filtered HNSW + int8 Quantization + Reranker
learningJourney.explanation: To keep 1536-dim HNSW indexes affordable in RAM, production clusters (Qdrant, OpenSearch, pgvector) apply **int8 scalar quantization** (4x RAM reduction) and oversample top-100 candidates before rescoring with full float32 vectors or a cross-encoder.

options.text: Because RRF runs the cross-encoder inside HNSW

options.text: Because RRF eliminates the need for an inverted index

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
